messages:
alex: uploaded a perfetto trace comparing batched vs streaming kernel selection — link: https://perfetto.local/trace/1767000000 (devbox). noticed selector flips from optimized_matmul -> generic_gemm after ~2 batches, and CPU scheduling spikes line up with KV cache misses.

rachel: quick q — this was the small-batch microbenchmark or an end-to-end request?

alex: microbench harness (seq=512, batch=4 -> burst to 16). end-to-end showed same pattern but noisier. attaching short snippet from the trace: 

--- perfetto notes ---
kernel_selector: choose_optimal() @ 00:00:12.342
kernel_selector: fallback choose_generic() @ 00:00:12.412 (latency +8ms)
thread: runtime-sched woke up 18x while kv_prefetch() pending
--- end ---

vikram: ran perf on the same harness with stacks:
```bash
# reproduce
perf record -F 99 -g -- ./bench_tokens --seq 512 --batch 4 --iters 200
perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
./flamegraph.pl out.folded > perf-flame.svg
```
flame highlights: ~24% in Python:tokenize_pipeline, ~18% in runtime.scheduler.spin_yield, ~12% syscalls waiting on kv_prefetch.

sam: can you paste the top collapsed stacks (text)? small sample ok

vikram: top few lines from out.folded:
```
python3:tokenize_pipeline;libc:memcpy 240
runtime:scheduler:spin_wait;kernel:do_futex 180
kvstore:fetch_prefetch;runtime:io_wait 120
python3:tokenize_pipeline;python3:decode_bytes 90
```

alex: interesting — tokenize_pipeline shows up high. that's the Python overhead we suspected when batch size small and tokenizer runs per-request.

sam: hypothesis: when kernel_selector sees low steady-state token rate it prefers lower-memory, generic kernels which are slower per-token but cheaper. the extra time increases scheduler wakeups and lets Python stacks dominate. try forcing selector to pick fast kernel for first N batches.

lee: config suggestion: bump kernel_selector.warmup_threshold from 8 -> 2 for short-burst workloads, and enable kv_prefetch:on_first_token=true. quick diff: 
```diff
- kernel_selector.warmup_threshold=8
+ kernel_selector.warmup_threshold=2
+ kv_prefetch.on_first_token=true
```

ci-bot: ran A/B microbench with changes on devbox:
- baseline (warmup=8): p50 latency=24.2ms, throughput=420 req/s
- tweak (warmup=2 + kv_prefetch): p50 latency=18.9ms, throughput=520 req/s
full run: https://ci.internal/runs/1767000000/compare

rachel: nice delta. any regression risk for long-running large-batch jobs?

vikram: I ran a 10k-iter large-batch sim (batch=64) with tweak — no measurable regression, selector still moves to large-kernel after steady-state. need to validate memory pressure on GPUs though.

sam: next steps: (1) run perf+flamegraph on a 1h soak with tweak, (2) capture nsys GPU kernel timeline at rollout candidate, (3) add unit test for selector heuristic covering bursty workloads. tagging @lee to own rollout plan.

alex: assigned: lee -> rollout plan, vikram -> 1h perf soak + flame, sam -> add selector unit tests, rachel -> coordinate staging run. I'll open a short RFC with the perfetto snippets and config patch.

lee: ack, will push a short RFC and a canary job. planning to start canary tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: note: automated benchmark run scheduled 2026-07-14T09:00Z (run id 176700-AB12). results will post to the compare link above.

alex: thanks all — good triage. we'll iterate if the soak shows new hotspots (especially Python tokenize).
